title: Composable pin selectors: tag / semver / commit resolution + upgrade safety
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Problem statement: customers need predictable model resolution when they declare a pin in the Redwood API or SDK. Current behavior supports a simple string pin but is underspecified for mixed selectors (tag names, semver ranges, commit hashes) and ambiguous when multiple matching variants (quantized vs float, hardware-optimized builds) exist. This ticket defines a composable pin selector surface, resolution precedence, validation rules, and runtime telemetry to keep applications stable while enabling safe upgrades.

Goals: 1) Define an expressive but ergonomic pin selector grammar that supports: exact commit (sha-like), stable tag names (eg. 'stable', 'redwood-verified'), semver exact and ranges (eg. '1.4.2', '^1.4', '>=1.4 <2.0'). 2) Specify how pinned selectors resolve to a single model artifact at request time and during rollouts, including deterministic tie-breakers for identical versions built for different runtimes (cpu/gpu/quantized). 3) Add SDK-side validation and warnings to prevent silent resolution surprises (eg. unbounded semver ranges in production). 4) Ensure runtime fallback and safety: a pinned request should not automatically start using a newer major unless explicitly allowed by selector. 5) Emit telemetry and auditing for every resolution decision to help troubleshooting and support upgrade policies.

Non-goals: do not implement a new package registry for models; do not change existing model publishing flows. This ticket only defines selector semantics and SDK surface + runtime resolver contract.
acceptance_criteria: Spec document added to Confluence describing selector grammar, precedence table, and deterministic tie-break rules
SDK parser implemented with unit tests for string selectors and structured selectors (examples provided)
Runtime resolver respects precedence matrix and logs full resolution path in trace/metadata
Backward compatibility: existing simple string pins continue to work as before (mapped to exact-match semantics)
E2E tests in infra/canary verify that 'semver range + pin' does not auto-upgrade major versions without explicit selector allowing it
Telemetry events emitted for resolution decisions and included in Console model-resolution trace view
implementation_notes: Selector grammar: allow three top-level syntaxes: commit sha (40 hex), tagged name (alphanumeric + dash), semver expression (semver library grammar). SDK will try to detect type by pattern before server-side validation.

Precedence: Exact commit > Exact semver (1.2.3) > Semver range (e.g. ^1.2.0) > Tag (most recent matching). Within same version number, prefer runtime-compatible build (gpu > cpu > cpu-quantized) according to customer region/runtime availability.

Structured selector example (SDK): {"selector_type":"semver","expr":"^1.4","allow_prerelease":false,"max_patch":2}  -- note: SDK will surface a typed builder but API accepts string equivalents for backwards compatibility.

Warnings: SDK will raise a non-failing warning if a semver range is used in production environment variable and the project has an explicit 'lockfile' present. Console will show a red flag for unbounded ranges linked to the route.

Runtime: resolver performs two-phase resolution: 1) catalog query to find candidate artifacts that match selector, 2) deterministic tie-break and check against deployability (region/capability). If no candidate is deployable, resolver returns a clear error with recommended fallback (eg. 'use tag stable or commit hash')
Telemetry: include fields resolution.selector, resolution.candidates_count, resolution.final_artifact, resolution.tie_break_reason, resolution.timestamp, request.route_id

Migration: existing pins without explicit syntax will be treated as 'legacy-string' and remain exact-match. Provide migration CLI to convert legacy pins to explicit semver selectors where appropriate.
open_questions: Do we allow a 'prefer-stable' annotation on semver ranges to prefer releases that have a 'stable' tag?
Should the runtime allow automatic minor upgrades within a pinned major except when 'lockfile' exists, or should we always require explicit selector for upgrades?
How should we represent 'build flavor' (quantized vs float) in selector language without making the grammar too verbose? Consider a separate 'constraints' field on the route config.
What rate of telemetry sampling is acceptable for high-volume customers to avoid cost blowup?
comments: 2025-02-11 - Miguel Torres: Initial spike done. Implemented prototype parser in sdk-js branch 'pin-selectors-spike'. Found semver lib mismatch between node and runtime go lib; added proposal to use semver.org compatible grammar.
2025-02-12 - Priya Menon (PM): Prefer conservative defaults for production; strongly recommend locking majors by default. See PM notes in Confluence.

2025-02-14 - Rui Chen (Runtime): Runtime candidate query needs indexing for 'tags' column to avoid full table scan on catalog. Filed ENG-56201 to add index. Marking as dependency for performance at scale.
2025-02-16 - Design review: UX for pin warnings accepted. Console will show a 'pin stability' badge and link to migration guide. Design attaches mock: https://drive.google.com/mock-pin-ui
2025-02-18 - Code review: PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/412 opened with parser and tests. Awaiting runtime resolver contract changes before merging.
